summary: Shinobu Arai Apple works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under Mark Csikszentmihalyi in 2000, doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003), and academic adviser Robert Bickner.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Nagoya University in 1995. She taught Sayaka Sonoda and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Shinsho Hanayama (1898–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He taught Buddhism there (~1935–1959) and held posts at Toyo University and Kokugakuin University.

Shinshu Kusumoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura. He also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shintaro Kitano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He was a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai (1912–1989) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Moriyama (born 1972) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed a master's at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and a doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2002–2006), later joining Shinshu University (~2009).
Shinya Yasutomi (1944–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1963–1967). He served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1993 to 2010.

Shiro Matsumoto (born 1950) studied Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He became a professor at Komazawa University and was a visiting professor at the University of Chicago.

Shivaram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Shankashastri Marulkar, and Maheshwarshastri Joshi. He served as professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University and headed Deccan College's Sanskrit Dictionary Department.

Shizuka Sasaki (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1975–1985) under Jikido Takasaki. He served as Professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University from circa 1992 to 2021.

Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg University (~1926–1930) and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1952–1977).
Shobha Rani Dash specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was an open-call researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010 and a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012).

Shodo Fujita (born 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Eshō Mikogami and Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

Shodo Yamagami (born 1939) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1962–1964) and served as an associate professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1977–2010).

Shogo Watanabe (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University (~1973–1982), where he later served on the faculty (attested 1991) and as professor (~2002–2019).

Shohaku Okumura (born 1948) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1968–1972) and under Kosho Uchiyama (1972–1975). He held posts at Minnesota Zen Meditation Center and the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center.

Shoji Mori (born 1938) studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi. He worked at the Okura Institute for the Study of Spiritual Culture and served as associate professor (~1978–1985) and professor (~1985–2009) at Toyo University.
Shoju Inaba (1915–1990) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Otani University (~1957–1980) and served as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.

Shojun Bando (1932–2004) studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1956). He held posts at Otani University, served as associate professor at Komazawa University (~1970–1978), and worked at Ueno Gakuen University (~1978–1998).
